decisions.rationale: "Classical galactosemia" names one specific disease, and the guidelines say to keep "classical" because it marks a particular form of the disease. It is the title mention.
Duplicate mention of the same specific disease in the abstract body, and the guidelines require all duplicate mentions to be annotated.
"deficiency" is a very general term. It refers to enzyme activity loss rather than naming a disease, so it is excluded.
"disorder" is a general, anaphoric term for the disease, comparable to the excluded general term "disease", so it is not annotated.
"galactosemia" is a named disease used as the disease concept in this passage. It is treated as one specific disease, though it could be read as a broader class covering several galactosemia forms.
